              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg2.l23.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">23:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg2.l23.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">return</span><span id="alg2.l23.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><math id="alg2.l23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(C,p_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" maxsize="0.800em" minsize="0.800em">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.800em">C</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.800em">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.800em">p</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathsize="0.800em">s</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" maxsize="0.800em" minsize="0.800em">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(C,p_{s})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="alg2.l23.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
</span>
</div>
</div>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Contour-Ext adds a knob to the surface when Contour-Explore stalls. It uses four
parts of Contour-Explore: the knob registry, the lowering, the legality checks,
and the evaluator. Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 3.5. Extending the Mapping Surface ‣ 3. Design ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows one invocation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Analysis of the stalled plan.</span>
Contour-Explore passes Contour-Ext the stalled plan <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="S3.SS5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>
(<math id="S3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>), the search history, the hashes of measured programs, and earlier
rejected knobs (<math id="S3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>). In <span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS5.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="12.45" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-1.77px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 12.45 12.45" width="12.45"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,12.45) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(6.23,0) translate(0,6.23)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#00838F;" fill="#00838F"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 6.23 0 C 6.23 3.44 3.44 6.23 0 6.23 C -3.44 6.23 -6.23 3.44 -6.23 0 C -6.23 -3.44 -3.44 -6.23 0 -6.23 C 3.44 -6.23 6.23 -3.44 6.23 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -3.98 -4.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="7.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS5.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">1</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span> diagnosis, an LLM-based extension
agent examines <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> without editing code. It reads the assembly, with each
instruction tagged by the lowering step that produced it, and an emulator
profile of memory traffic and unit occupancy. It ends with a bottleneck
report <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> that cites measurements and code locations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implementation of a new knob.</span>
In <span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS5.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="12.45" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-1.77px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 12.45 12.45" width="12.45"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,12.45) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(6.23,0) translate(0,6.23)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#6A1B9A;" fill="#6A1B9A"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 6.23 0 C 6.23 3.44 3.44 6.23 0 6.23 C -3.44 6.23 -6.23 3.44 -6.23 0 C -6.23 -3.44 -3.44 -6.23 0 -6.23 C 3.44 -6.23 6.23 -3.44 6.23 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -3.98 -4.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="7.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">2</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span> proposal, the agent specifies one knob that addresses <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>
and differs from every entry in <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>: its values with the default first, the
lowering change for each value, and the operator families it applies to.
In <span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS5.p3.pic2" class="ltx_picture" height="12.45" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-1.77px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 12.45 12.45" width="12.45"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,12.45) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(6.23,0) translate(0,6.23)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#B35900;" fill="#B35900"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 6.23 0 C 6.23 3.44 3.44 6.23 0 6.23 C -3.44 6.23 -6.23 3.44 -6.23 0 C -6.23 -3.44 -3.44 -6.23 0 -6.23 C 3.44 -6.23 6.23 -3.44 6.23 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -3.98 -4.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="7.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.pic2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">3</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span> implementation, the agent registers the knob with a
derivation rule and a legality predicate, and implements its values in the
schedule layer. It cannot change the computation, instruction selection, or
the evaluator. Before submission, it can compile and emulate plans through
the Contour-Explore resolver and evaluator.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Correctness and effectiveness.</span>
Contour-Ext accepts a knob only if it passes two groups of checks. The
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS5.p4.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="12.45" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-1.77px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 12.45 12.45" width="12.45"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,12.45) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(6.23,0) translate(0,6.23)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#C62828;" fill="#C62828"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 6.23 0 C 6.23 3.44 3.44 6.23 0 6.23 C -3.44 6.23 -6.23 3.44 -6.23 0 C -6.23 -3.44 -3.44 -6.23 0 -6.23 C 3.44 -6.23 6.23 -3.44 6.23 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -3.98 -4.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="7.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS5.p4.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">4</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span> correctness checks require that the default value reproduces
the programs of the previous compiler version at <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, that each
new value changes the program, and that each new value keeps the output
error within the numerical bound of the target. The <span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S3.SS5.p4.pic2" class="ltx_picture" height="12.45" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-1.77px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 12.45 12.45" width="12.45"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,12.45) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(6.23,0) translate(0,6.23)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#2E7D32;" fill="#2E7D32"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 6.23 0 C 6.23 3.44 3.44 6.23 0 6.23 C -3.44 6.23 -6.23 3.44 -6.23 0 C -6.23 -3.44 -3.44 -6.23 0 -6.23 C 3.44 -6.23 6.23 -3.44 6.23 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -3.98 -4.46)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.5em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="8.92" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 8.92)" width="7.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS5.p4.pic2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">5</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span> effectiveness checks run hill climbing on the extended surface <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> from
<math id="S3.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. Its best plan <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> must use the new knob, its program must not be
reachable without the knob, and it must be faster than <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> by a gain
threshold. The new values must also meet the numerical bound at <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> on
inputs with large magnitudes and outliers. A failed check returns its
reason to the agent, which revises the patch or proposes another knob; each
rejected knob is added to <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Return to Contour-Explore.</span>
An accepted knob becomes part of a new compiler version. Contour-Explore
publishes the extended surface and resumes search from <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>; its search
policies use the new knob in the same way as any other knob. When Contour-Ext
returns no knob, Contour-Explore continues with the previous compiler version.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Evaluation</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span>Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use Gemmini to evaluate Contour-Explore
(Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2. Contour-Explore on Gemmini ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), VTA with TVM and AutoTVM to evaluate
Contour-Ext (Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3. Contour-Ext on VTA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>), and PLENA to evaluate the full
system (Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Accelerator platforms.</span>
We evaluate <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Contour</span> on Gemmini, VTA, and PLENA. For Gemmini, we use the
<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GemminiRocketConfig</span> provided by Chipyard
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amid et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Genc et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, whose default Gemmini configuration sets
<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">DIM=16</span> and instantiates a <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 16</annotation></semantics></math> systolic array. We build the
bitstream of this SoC with Vivado 2022.2, generate its software image with
PetaLinux 2022.2, and deploy the resulting system on a Xilinx ZC706 FPGA
evaluation board. We obtain Gemmini performance measurements from this
physical implementation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For VTA, we use the TVM Versatile Tensor Accelerator
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Moreau et al., 2019</a>)</cite> and measure cycles with tsim, which simulates its
Chisel RTL with Verilator. The evaluator compares each output element by
element with a CPU reference.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For PLENA, we use the authors’ official RTL release and the transaction-level
mode of their official simulator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">AICrossSim, 2026</a>)</cite>. The
simulator executes compiled assembly against an explicit memory layout and
produces both numerical outputs and simulated latency.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Models and workloads.</span>
All main experiments use DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeepSeek-AI, 2026</a>)</cite>, with the same model settings across
the compared LLM methods; the extension agent of Contour-Ext uses the same
model.
On Gemmini and PLENA, we adopt the workload
definitions and input shapes from KernelCraft <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Each workload–input-shape combination is a <em id="S4.SS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">workload instance</em>.
Within each workload family, C1, C3, and C5 denote the smallest,
middle-sized, and largest workloads, respectively.
The evaluation covers 20 Gemmini instances and
18 PLENA instances: FFN, SwiGLU, FlashAttention, MHA, GQA,
and MQA, each with shapes C1, C3, and C5. These multi-stage workloads
exercise fusion and attention computations beyond standalone GEMM and GEMV.
On VTA, we use 16 int8 instances with int32 accumulation, shift, and
clipping: FFN (two dense layers with ReLU), GEMM, and GEMV, each with shapes
C1–C5 from smallest to largest, and the fully connected layer of ResNet-18
(R18). AutoTVM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2018b</a>)</cite> tunes the knobs of a hand-written
TVM schedule template. The TVM 0.12 VTA dense template exposes tile sizes
for the batch, input-channel, and output-channel dimensions and the number
of virtual threads over output channels; we call the mappings expressible by
these knobs the <em id="S4.SS1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">AutoTVM surface</em>. The <em id="S4.SS1.p5.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Contour-Ext surface</em> of an
instance adds the knobs that Contour-Ext accepts on it. Hill climbing runs on
the AutoTVM surface until it stalls; Contour-Ext then extends the surface from
that stall, and hill climbing continues on the Contour-Ext surface. We also run
the AutoTVM XGBTuner, GATuner, and RandomTuner on both surfaces with up to
512 measurements per run and report the median of three seeds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Search agents and baselines.</span>
Our <em id="S4.SS1.p6.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">naive agent</em> follows the feedback-directed loop in Section <a href="#S3" title="3. Design ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>:
an LLM proposes a mapping intent, receives correctness and performance
feedback, and uses that feedback to propose the next intent. We denote
this configuration Naive + Contour-Explore. Contour-Explore
retains the fastest verified kernel found during the run.
We also connect hill climbing and a genetic algorithm (GA) to the same
interface. These policies share the mapping surface,
symbolic completion, code generation, and evaluator.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">KernelCraft generates kernels without a supplied starting
kernel and provides the ISA-level generation baseline. Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1. Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> evaluates the AccelOpt optimization harness through Contour-Explore and at the program level.
We also report the software shipped with each accelerator: Gemmini’s
library matrix-multiply routine (<span id="S4.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">tiled_matmul_auto</span> in
<span id="S4.SS1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemmini.h</span>) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Genc et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, which we call the Gemmini
library, and the PLENA compiler <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">AICrossSim, 2026</a>)</cite>, which compiles each
instance once without search.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Search budgets and reporting.</span>
Contour-Explore search permits up to 80 candidate evaluations per PLENA
instance and 12 unique candidate evaluations per Gemmini instance.
On PLENA, hill climbing and GA use all 80 evaluations. The naive agent
can stop earlier: its run is also bounded in the number of LLM turns and
requests, and those that repair a rejected intent or yield no new candidate
consume this bound without an evaluation. We report the evaluation counts.
Methods with three runs report the median
latency for each instance. Token usage and evaluation counts are averaged
across the runs. The naive agent uses three runs per instance. On PLENA, GA uses three runs and hill climbing uses one; on Gemmini, hill climbing and GA use 1,000 seeds per instance. KernelCraft uses three runs per instance.
To extend the PLENA surfaces, hill climbing runs in iterations of 16
evaluations and invokes Contour-Ext when the relative improvement over the last
six iterations is below 0.2%. The effectiveness checks run 40 evaluations of
hill climbing and require a gain of at least 1%. The extension of an
instance ends after three consecutive rejected invocations, eight accepted
knobs, 4,000 evaluations, or 48 hours.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Metrics.</span>
We report geometric-mean speedup over a reference kernel, which is the
Gemmini library on Gemmini and <span id="S4.SS1.p9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> on VTA and PLENA, and verified
coverage, the fraction of instances for which a method returns a verified
kernel. <em id="S4.SS1.p9.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Tokens per verified kernel</em> equal the total prompt and
completion tokens across all runs divided by the number of runs that
return a verified kernel. Failed runs contribute their token usage to
the numerator. Each run contributes at most one kernel to the denominator.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">We define <em id="S4.SS1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">disappointment</em> on an instance as
<math id="S4.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=1-t_{\mathrm{best}}/t_{\mathrm{method}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>best</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>method</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=1-t_{\mathrm{best}}/t_{\mathrm{method}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where
<math id="S4.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{method}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>method</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{method}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the latency returned by the method and
<math id="S4.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{best}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>best</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{best}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the best latency known for the instance. On
Gemmini, it is the lowest latency that the naive agent, hill climbing, or GA
finds in any run, so a method outside these three can have negative
disappointment; on PLENA, it is the lowest latency among the compared
methods and the longer search runs on the merged Contour-Ext surface
(Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>).
A method that returns no verified kernel has <math id="S4.SS1.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=100\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
We report mean disappointment across instances.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span>Contour-Explore on Gemmini</h3>

<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.00894v4/gemmini_search_results.svg" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/172;" width="476" height="172"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4. </span>Gemmini results on 20 instances: (a) cycles normalized to the
Gemmini library (dashed line); (b) disappointment. Crosses:
KernelCraft failures. BMM: BatchMatMul.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison.</span>
We compare the kernels found by the naive agent, hill climbing, and GA
through Contour-Explore with the Gemmini library and with KernelCraft
across 20 instances from BatchMatMul, GEMM, GEMV, and Linear. Every kernel
uses the same workload inputs,
correctness oracle, and execution boundary. The naive agent, hill
climbing, GA, and KernelCraft have the same evaluation budget of 12
evaluations per instance. We also compare verified coverage and tokens per
verified kernel against KernelCraft.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Search through Contour-Explore against the hand-written library.</span>
Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2. Contour-Explore on Gemmini ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>a normalizes cycles to the Gemmini library,
the kernel that a Gemmini user obtains without search.
With 12 evaluations, the naive agent returns a faster kernel than the
library on 19 of the 20 instances, and its kernels are <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.17\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.17</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster
in geometric mean. The gain holds in every workload family: <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.30\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.30</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.30\times</annotation></semantics></math> on
BatchMatMul, <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.18\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.18</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.18\times</annotation></semantics></math> on GEMV, <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.15\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.15</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.15\times</annotation></semantics></math> on GEMM, and <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.06\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.06</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.06\times</annotation></semantics></math> on
Linear, where the library is 0.4% faster on Linear C4. Under the same
budget, hill climbing and GA are <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.17\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.17</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.10\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.10\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than
the library. Mean disappointment is 4.9% for both the naive agent and hill
climbing, 10.7% for GA, and 18.2% for the library: every policy is closer
on average than the library to the best kernel found on the surface.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Verified coverage and kernel quality.</span>
KernelCraft returns a verified kernel on 12 of the 20 instances
(60%). On the other eight, none of the programs that it generates within
its budget compiles and passes the correctness check; we count these
instances as failures. The naive agent through Contour-Explore returns a
verified kernel on all 20 instances in each run.
On the 12 instances with a verified KernelCraft result, the naive
agent’s kernels are <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.86\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.86</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.86\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than KernelCraft’s in
geometric mean, and KernelCraft’s kernels are slower than the
Gemmini library on all 12, by <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.44\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.44</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.44\times</annotation></semantics></math> in geometric mean.
This performance comparison is conditioned on KernelCraft success;
the coverage comparison includes the entire suite.
The naive agent returns a faster kernel than KernelCraft on every instance; mean disappointment is 78.6% for KernelCraft, including its eight failures at 100% (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2. Contour-Explore on Gemmini ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>b).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cost per verified kernel.</span>
Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reports 564K tokens per verified
kernel for the naive agent through Contour-Explore, compared with 765K for
KernelCraft, a 26.3% reduction. The denominator accounts for the
KernelCraft runs that consume tokens without returning a
verified kernel. Coverage from the compiler default and verified incumbent
selection converts search expenditure into a usable result on every instance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3. </span>Contour-Ext on VTA</h3>

<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.00894v4/vta_ext_results.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/174;" width="476" height="174" aria-label="Two side-by-side bar charts over 16 VTA instances with a
logarithmic y-axis, one for hill climbing and one for XGBTuner. In both,
bars on the Contour-Ext surface are far
below the bars on the AutoTVM surface on FFN and GEMM, and slightly below
them on GEMV and the ResNet-18 layer."><p>Two side-by-side bar charts over 16 VTA instances with a
logarithmic y-axis, one for hill climbing and one for XGBTuner. In both,
bars on the Contour-Ext surface are far
below the bars on the AutoTVM surface on FFN and GEMM, and slightly below
them on GEMV and the ResNet-18 layer.</p></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5. </span>VTA results on 16 instances: cycles normalized to
<span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> (log scale). XGBTuner reports the median of three seeds.<span id="acmlabel2" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay">Two side-by-side bar charts over 16 VTA instances with a
logarithmic y-axis, one for hill climbing and one for XGBTuner. In both,
bars on the Contour-Ext surface are far
below the bars on the AutoTVM surface on FFN and GEMM, and slightly below
them on GEMV and the ResNet-18 layer.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Hill climbing on the AutoTVM surface stalls at a <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.84\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.84</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.84\times</annotation></semantics></math> geometric-mean
speedup over <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>, which on VTA is the kernel compiled from the
default configuration of the TVM template. All 32 Contour-Ext invocations, two per
instance, are accepted; they use 3.60M tokens in total, or 112K tokens per
invocation. On the resulting Contour-Ext surface, hill climbing reaches
<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="7.77\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.77</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.77\times</annotation></semantics></math>, and its final cycles are <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4.22\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.22</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.22\times</annotation></semantics></math> lower than at the stall
in geometric mean (Figure <a href="#acmlabel2" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3. Contour-Ext on VTA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>a). The largest speedups occur on
FFN and GEMM, at <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="18.83\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>18.83</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18.83\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="14.10\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.10\times</annotation></semantics></math> over <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>; GEMV
and R18 reach <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.17\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.17</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.17\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.78\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.78</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.78\times</annotation></semantics></math>. The most frequent added knobs
move operand loads out of inner loops, followed by knobs for loop order and
tiling. The added knobs also improve search procedures that were not used to
find them. XGBTuner reaches <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.85\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.85</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.85\times</annotation></semantics></math> over <span id="S4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> on the AutoTVM
surface and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="7.66\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7.66</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.66\times</annotation></semantics></math> on the Contour-Ext surface, so its kernels are
<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4.14\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.14\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster on the Contour-Ext surface
(Figure <a href="#acmlabel2" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3. Contour-Ext on VTA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>b), and GATuner and RandomTuner also reach fewer
cycles on the Contour-Ext surface on all 16 instances. On FFN, most tuner
measurements on the AutoTVM surface fail because many tile combinations are
illegal; for XGBTuner with seed 1, the failure rate is 99.6% on FFN C4.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4. </span>Full System on PLENA</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On PLENA, we first measure how far Contour-Ext raises the performance that
search can reach on the surface, and then evaluate Contour-Explore on the
final surface against KernelCraft.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.00894v4/plena_ext_surface.svg" id="S4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/360;" width="476" height="360" aria-label="Eighteen small step plots in a grid of three shapes by six
workload families. In each plot, the curve on the base surface stays near
one, the curve on the per-instance Contour-Ext surface drops after accepted
knobs, and the curve on the merged surface drops early and ends lowest on
most instances."><p>Eighteen small step plots in a grid of three shapes by six
workload families. In each plot, the curve on the base surface stays near
one, the curve on the per-instance Contour-Ext surface drops after accepted
knobs, and the curve on the merged surface drops early and ends lowest on
most instances.</p></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6. </span>Best latency so far on 18 PLENA instances, normalized to
<span id="S4.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>: base surface (w/o Contour-Ext), per-instance Contour-Ext
surface (w/ Contour-Ext; dotted lines mark accepted knobs), and merged
Contour-Ext surface (pooled).<span id="acmlabel3" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay">Eighteen small step plots in a grid of three shapes by six
workload families. In each plot, the curve on the base surface stays near
one, the curve on the per-instance Contour-Ext surface drops after accepted
knobs, and the curve on the merged surface drops early and ends lowest on
most instances.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Contour-Ext raises the reachable performance.</span>
We call the surface that the surface generator publishes for an instance its
<em id="S4.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">base surface</em>. On the base surface, hill climbing reaches a
<math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.048\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.048</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.048\times</annotation></semantics></math> geometric-mean speedup over <span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> after 3,000
evaluations per instance, and it improves <span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> by less than 3%
on 14 of the 18 instances (Figure <a href="#acmlabel3" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). Contour-Ext is
invoked 119 times across the 18 instances and accepts 47 knobs, using 2.30B
tokens in total, or 19.3M tokens per invocation. With the same 3,000
evaluations, hill climbing on each instance’s Contour-Ext surface reaches
<math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.191\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.191</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.191\times</annotation></semantics></math>. FlashAttention gains the most, from <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.229\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.229</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.229\times</annotation></semantics></math> on the base
surface to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.935\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.935</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.935\times</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A knob definition derives its values from the workload, so a knob accepted
on one instance can be published on the others. We merge the knobs accepted
on the 18 instances into one surface with 30 knob definitions after
removing duplicates; <span id="S4.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> is the same program on all surfaces.
On this <em id="S4.SS4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">merged Contour-Ext surface</em>, hill climbing reaches <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.262\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.262</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.262\times</annotation></semantics></math>
after 3,000 evaluations (median of three seeds), which is
<math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.20\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.20</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.20\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than its result on the base surface, and <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.157\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.157</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.157\times</annotation></semantics></math> after the
first 80 evaluations. The merged surface reaches at least the speedup of the
instance’s own Contour-Ext surface on 17 of the 18 instances. On GQA C5, where
Contour-Ext accepted no knob, it raises the speedup from <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.017\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.017</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.017\times</annotation></semantics></math> to
<math id="S4.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.135\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.135</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.135\times</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Contour-Explore on the merged surface.</span>
We run the naive agent, hill climbing, and GA through
Contour-Explore on the merged Contour-Ext surface with the 80-evaluation budget and
compare them with KernelCraft and the PLENA compiler
(Figure <a href="#acmlabel4" title="Figure 7 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>,
Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Disappointment is measured against the best known
latency on the merged surface, found by the longer runs in
Figure <a href="#acmlabel3" title="Figure 6 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, which reach <math id="S4.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.269\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.269</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.269\times</annotation></semantics></math> speed-up over
<span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.00894v4/plena_search_results.png" id="S4.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/275;" width="476" height="275" alt="Two bar charts over 18 PLENA instances for the naive agent,
hill climbing, GA, the PLENA compiler, and KernelCraft. The naive agent has
the lowest latency on most instances and disappointment near zero; the PLENA
compiler is slower than Candidate-0 on 16 instances; KernelCraft
fails on 13 instances.">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7. </span>PLENA results on the merged Contour-Ext surface (18 instances):
(a) latency normalized to <span id="S4.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> (dashed line); (b)
disappointment. Crosses: KernelCraft failures. Hill: first 80
evaluations of one run.<span id="acmlabel4" class="ltx_acm_description ltx_centering ltx_nodisplay">Two bar charts over 18 PLENA instances for the naive agent,
hill climbing, GA, the PLENA compiler, and KernelCraft. The naive agent has
the lowest latency on most instances and disappointment near zero; the PLENA
compiler is slower than Candidate-0 on 16 instances; KernelCraft
fails on 13 instances.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Search efficiency.</span>
The naive agent improves <span id="S4.SS4.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> on all 18 instances and reaches a
<math id="S4.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.243\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.243</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.243\times</annotation></semantics></math> geometric-mean speedup with a mean of 67.9 evaluations per
instance. Its mean disappointment is 2.1%, and its disappointment
is below 3% on 15
instances; on MHA C1, it finds a kernel 0.4% faster than the best
one from the longer runs. Hill climbing and GA reach <math id="S4.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.157\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.157</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.157\times</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S4.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.139\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.139</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.139\times</annotation></semantics></math>, with mean disappointment of 8.3% and 10.1%; the naive
agent’s kernels are 7.4% and 9.1% faster than theirs in geometric mean.
Among the three policies, the naive agent returns the lowest latency
on 15 instances. The largest gaps occur on FlashAttention C3 and C5, where
hill climbing has 30.2% and 31.9% disappointment after 80 evaluations and the
naive agent has 4.1% and 1.6%.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2. </span>Contour-Explore search policies on the merged Contour-Ext surface (18
PLENA instances). Evaluations: mean per instance, with a budget of 80.</figcaption>

<td id="S4.T2.2.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.2.4.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">80.0</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with KernelCraft.</span>
KernelCraft returns a verified kernel on 5 of the 18 instances and
fails on the other 13 by the criterion of Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2. Contour-Explore on Gemmini ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>,
while every policy through Contour-Explore returns one on all 18. On these five
instances, KernelCraft reaches <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.045\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.045</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.045\times</annotation></semantics></math> over <span id="S4.SS4.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>
with 13.0% mean disappointment, and the naive agent reaches <math id="S4.SS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.181\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.181</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.181\times</annotation></semantics></math> with
1.8%; the naive agent is faster on all five. Pooling tokens over all runs,
the naive agent uses 1.393M tokens per verified kernel and
KernelCraft uses 8.375M, an 83.4% reduction
(Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with the PLENA compiler.</span>
The speedups above are measured over <span id="S4.SS4.p7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>, and <span id="S4.SS4.p7.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>
is itself faster than the PLENA compiler on 16 of the 18 instances: the
compiler’s programs reach <math id="S4.SS4.p7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0.849\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.849</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.849\times</annotation></semantics></math> the speed of <span id="S4.SS4.p7.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> in
geometric mean. The two exceptions are FlashAttention C3 and C5, where the
compiler skips key blocks that the causal mask excludes entirely and
<span id="S4.SS4.p7.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> computes them. Every policy through Contour-Explore returns a
faster kernel than the compiler on all 18 instances, including these two,
and the naive agent’s kernels are <math id="S4.SS4.p7.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.46\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.46</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.46\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster in geometric mean
(Figure <a href="#acmlabel4" title="Figure 7 ‣ 4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3. </span>Tokens per verified kernel. Both methods use three runs per
instance.</figcaption>
<table id="S4.T3.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S4.T3.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T3.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Platform</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Naive + Contour-Explore</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">KernelCraft</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Reduction</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S4.T3.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T3.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Gemmini (20)</span></th>
<td id="S4.T3.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">564K</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">765K</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.2.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">26.3%</span></td></tr>

<td id="S4.T3.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">1.393M</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.2.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">8.375M</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.2.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.2.3.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">83.4%</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Discussion</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1. </span>Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine whether changing the model improves program-level generation
and search through Contour-Explore. The Gemmini ablation compares Flash and Pro
within the DeepSeek-V4 family; the PLENA experiments extend the comparison
to GPT-6.1-Sol (Sol), separating generation success
from the performance of verified kernels.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gemmini: limited gains from Flash to Pro.</span>
We retain six instances selected from the Flash results to span easy,
intermediate, and success-boundary cases. Each model–method pair reports
seed 1, with candidates replayed under the same board timing harness
(Figure <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.1. Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). For Naive + Contour-Explore, five instances
differ by at most 0.1%; Pro improves GEMM C4 by 4.7%. Across all six,
Pro lowers the geometric-mean cycle count by 0.8% while increasing API cost
by <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="17.0\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>17.0</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17.0\times</annotation></semantics></math>. KernelCraft’s response is mixed: Pro solves GEMV C3,
where Flash fails, but fails on Linear C4, which Flash solves. Among the five
instances solved by KernelCraft-Pro, Naive + Contour-Explore + Flash is
<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.60\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.60</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.60\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster in geometric mean. These results establish limited
benefit from this model upgrade on the tested Gemmini mappings.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.00894v4/gemmini_model_ablation.svg" id="S5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/165;" width="476" height="165"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8. </span>Gemmini Flash/Pro ablation: (a) Naive + Contour-Explore; (b) KernelCraft;
(c, d) cycles and API cost for KernelCraft-Pro versus Naive + Contour-Explore + Flash.
Crosses denote failures. BM/MM/MV/LN:
BatchMatMul/GEMM/GEMV/Linear.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PLENA: generation success and kernel quality.</span>
Following the evaluation protocol used above, we compare KernelCraft and
Naive + Contour-Explore with Sol on the 18 PLENA instances.
KernelCraft + Sol verifies 15 instances, versus 5 for DeepSeek-Flash
(median of three runs); Naive + Contour-Explore + Sol verifies all 18.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.1. Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> compares performance on the 15 instances
solved by KernelCraft + Sol. Even after excluding its failures, KernelCraft’s
geometric-mean speedup over <span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> is only <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0.894\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.894</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.894\times</annotation></semantics></math>.
Naive + Contour-Explore with the same model achieves
<math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.262\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.262</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.262\times</annotation></semantics></math> speedup on those same instances. Sol therefore
helps program-level generation solve previously unsuccessful workloads,
while the generated kernels collectively remain slower than the compiler
default and the mappings found through Contour-Explore.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4. </span>PLENA coverage on 18 instances; geometric-mean speedup
over <span id="S5.T4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> on the 15 instances solved by KernelCraft + Sol. Higher is better.</figcaption>
<table id="S5.T4.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S5.T4.4.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T4.4.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Method</span></th>
<th id="S5.T4.4.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Verified</span></th>
<th id="S5.T4.4.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Speedup <math id="S5.T4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math></span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S5.T4.4.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.4.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:90%;">Candidate-0</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">18/18</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.000\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">1.000</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" mathsize="0.900em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000\times</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T4.4.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.4.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">KernelCraft + Sol</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">15/18</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0.894\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">0.894</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" mathsize="0.900em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.894\times</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T4.4.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S5.T4.4.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Naive + Contour-Explore + Sol</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.4.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">18/18</span></td>
<td id="S5.T4.4.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="S5.T4.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.262\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">1.262</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" mathsize="0.900em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.262\times</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AccelOpt through Contour-Explore.</span>
AccelOpt is an LLM optimization harness with a planner, executor, and
summarizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>; we build on its public repository at
commit <span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">47e29a7</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">acc, 2026</a>)</cite>. Program-level AccelOpt edits
the kernel program, while AccelOpt through Contour-Explore proposes mapping
intents through the interface of Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2. Contour-Explore on Gemmini ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>; both start
from <span id="S5.SS1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>.
On the 20 Gemmini instances with DeepSeek-Flash, AccelOpt through
Contour-Explore returns a faster kernel than program-level AccelOpt on every
instance. Its kernels are <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.50\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.50</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.50\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster in geometric mean, mean
disappointment falls from 36.8% to 6.3%, and it uses 588K instead of 620K
tokens per instance. Program-level AccelOpt returns a faster kernel than
the Gemmini library on 4 of the 20 instances, and AccelOpt through
Contour-Explore on 17.
Contour-Explore uses three runs and program-level AccelOpt uses one.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PLENA: model choice within AccelOpt.</span>
We next compare DeepSeek-Flash and Sol within the AccelOpt harness on four
attention workloads: FlashAttention, MHA, GQA, and MQA, each at shape C3,
with one run per configuration.
AccelOpt + Sol tests whether a more capable model can complete the
program-level route without a compiler: it optimizes the kernels that
KernelCraft + Sol generates, whereas the other configurations start from
<span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>.
Within AccelOpt + Contour-Explore, replacing DeepSeek-Flash with Sol improves
all four instances (Figure <a href="#S5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 5.1. Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>): mean disappointment falls from 1.48% to 0.04%,
mean tokens fall from 1.83M to 0.68M (62.7% fewer), and geometric-mean
speedup over <span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> rises from <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.223\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.223</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.223\times</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.241\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.241</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.241\times</annotation></semantics></math>.
AccelOpt + Sol raises the geometric-mean speedup of its KernelCraft-generated
kernels over <span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> from <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0.771\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.771</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.771\times</annotation></semantics></math> before optimization to
<math id="S5.SS1.p6.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0.934\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.934</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.934\times</annotation></semantics></math> afterward, but retains 18.23% mean disappointment and uses
8.01M tokens per instance. <span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">With the same Sol model, AccelOpt + Contour-Explore
achieves 32.8% higher geometric-mean performance than this
program-level route at just 7.2% of
AccelOpt’s API cost ($1.52 versus $21.02 per instance).</span>
The benefit also holds for DeepSeek: Contour-Explore reduces mean disappointment
from 17.92% to 1.48%, raises the geometric-mean speedup over
<span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span> from <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.018\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.018</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.018\times</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.223\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.223</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.223\times</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.p6.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.20\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.20</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.20\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster
kernels), and uses 1.83M instead of 9.73M tokens per instance.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2608.00894v4/plena_model_ablation.svg" id="S5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/193;" width="476" height="193"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9. </span>AccelOpt on four PLENA attention instances (C3): (a)
disappointment; (b) tokens per run (bars) and API cost in USD (labels).
FA: FlashAttention.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Model capability thus remains useful on PLENA, both for generating correct
programs and for improving mapping search. The mapping interface preserves
that opportunity while providing a verified default that stronger models
can improve upon.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2. </span>Ablation of Contour-Ext</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We remove one mechanism of Contour-Ext at a time and repeat the extension loop
of Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> on four PLENA instances, FlashAttention C1,
SwiGLU C3, MHA C1, and FFN C1, with one run per configuration
(Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.2. Ablation of Contour-Ext ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). Without diagnosis, the extension agent
starts at the proposal phase and has no profiling tool. Without checks,
Contour-Ext keeps every patch that applies and compiles <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>, and
skips the correctness and effectiveness checks. Without failure feedback,
the history <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> of rejected knobs is empty at every invocation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5. </span>Ablation of Contour-Ext on four PLENA instances: accepted knobs
out of invocations and geometric-mean speedup over <span id="S5.T5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Candidate-0</span>.
<sup id="S5.T5.5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S5.T5.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup>Excluding the incorrect knob.</figcaption>
<table id="S5.T5.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S5.T5.6.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T5.6.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"><span id="S5.T5.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Configuration</span></th>

<td id="S5.T5.6.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:5.0pt;padding-right:5.0pt;"><span id="S5.T5.6.7.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">–</span></td>
