</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS2.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="15.32" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-2.91px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 15.32 15.32" width="15.32"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,15.32) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(7.66,0) translate(0,7.66)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#00838F;" fill="#00838F"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 7.66 0 C 7.66 4.23 4.23 7.66 0 7.66 C -4.23 7.66 -7.66 4.23 -7.66 0 C -7.66 -4.23 -4.23 -7.66 0 -7.66 C 4.23 -7.66 7.66 -4.23 7.66 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -6.02 -4.75)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.76em;--ltx-fo-height:0.6em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="9.49" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.49)" width="12.03"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S5.SS2.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">A</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposals need evidence.</span>
Diagnosis and failure feedback both tell the extension agent where to look:
the profile of the stalled program shows what limits it, and <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> shows what
has already failed. Without either, fewer proposals pass the checks, the
loop ends earlier, and the final kernels are slower
(Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.2. Ablation of Contour-Ext ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>); on FFN C1, no knob is accepted at all.
Without <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, the agent also proposes rejected knobs again more often. To find useful
knobs, the agent therefore needs measured bottlenecks and past failures in
addition to the lowering code.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS2.p3.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="14.78" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-2.65px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 14.78 14.78" width="14.78"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,14.78) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(7.39,0) translate(0,7.39)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#C62828;" fill="#C62828"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 7.39 0 C 7.39 4.08 4.08 7.39 0 7.39 C -4.08 7.39 -7.39 4.08 -7.39 0 C -7.39 -4.08 -4.08 -7.39 0 -7.39 C 4.08 -7.39 7.39 -4.08 7.39 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -5.66 -4.75)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.71em;--ltx-fo-height:0.6em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="9.49" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.49)" width="11.32"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S5.SS2.p3.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">B</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Without checks, an incorrect knob reaches the final kernel.</span>
Without the checks, Contour-Ext accepts a knob that skips writing an
intermediate result of FlashAttention C1 back to memory, although the
program later reads it. The program still passes the evaluator, because that
memory happens to hold valid values, and it is faster, so hill climbing
selects it for the final kernel. When memory is filled with NaN before
execution, its outputs contain NaN. Passing the evaluator during search does
not show that a knob is correct, so new knobs must be checked on additional
inputs before they enter the surface.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="S5.SS2.p4.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="14.86" overflow="visible" style="vertical-align:-2.68px" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 14.86 14.86" width="14.86"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,14.86) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0) translate(7.43,0) translate(0,7.43)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#2E7D32;" fill="#2E7D32"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 7.43 0 C 7.43 4.1 4.1 7.43 0 7.43 C -4.1 7.43 -7.43 4.1 -7.43 0 C -7.43 -4.1 -4.1 -7.43 0 -7.43 C 4.1 -7.43 7.43 -4.1 7.43 0 Z M 0 0"></path></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#FFFFFF;--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#FFFFFF" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 -5.75 -4.75)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:0.72em;--ltx-fo-height:0.6em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:11.5pt;" height="9.49" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.49)" width="11.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S5.SS2.p4.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">C</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Accepted knobs transfer across workloads.</span>
When the knobs that only the target instance contributed are removed from
the merged surface, the remaining knobs, all proposed for other instances,
still recover most of the gain of the instance’s own extension loop. On the
two attention instances, they recover all of it. The knobs that Contour-Ext
accepts are therefore reusable compiler capabilities that apply beyond the
workload they were proposed for, consistent with the merged surface in
Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4. Full System on PLENA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> matching or exceeding each instance’s own
surface on 17 of the 18 instances.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6. </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">KernelCraft generates ISA assembly for emerging accelerators, AutoComp
optimizes ISA-level C, and AccelOpt optimizes Trainium NKI kernels using
profiles and optimization memory
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hong et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>; GPU kernel
agents and benchmarks take the same program-level approach
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sereda et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liao et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. In these
workflows, the agent expresses its mapping choices through generated or
modified kernel code, which at the ISA level includes instruction calls,
address calculations, and data-movement schedules. In Contour-Explore, the agent
sets knob values and the compiler generates the kernel; the search policies
of these harnesses can use the same interface, as our AccelOpt integration
shows (Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1. Sensitivity to Model Capability and Optimization Harness ‣ 5. Discussion ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">AutoTVM tunes the knobs of developer-written schedule templates
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2018b</a>)</cite>, and Ansor and MetaSchedule generate schedule spaces
from fixed rules <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. Timeloop
constructs per-layer mapspaces from hand-written architecture descriptions
and scores mappings analytically <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Parashar et al., 2019</a>)</cite>. In these
systems, the space is fixed before search, and a mapping outside it is
unreachable for any search policy. Contour-Explore derives its mapping surface
from the RTL-lifted machine semantics and measures every mapping as a
generated kernel; when search stalls, Contour-Ext adds knobs and their lowering
to the compiler, extending the surface itself (Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3. Contour-Ext on VTA ‣ 4. Evaluation ‣ Contour: Extensible Mapping Surfaces for Agentic Accelerator Kernel Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Concurrent to our work, CAKE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2026</a>)</cite> proposes co-designing a GPU
compiler with kernel agents: agents write a typed, hardware-explicit
schedule IR, and the compiler returns localized diagnostics and evolves its
verifier rules and IR primitives when candidates expose missing
capabilities. Our work differs in three respects. First, CAKE targets NVIDIA
GPUs, for which large libraries of production kernels exist, and its
methodology builds on them: the IR is distilled from production kernels such
as those in FlashInfer and CUTLASS. Emerging accelerators have no such
corpus. Second, CAKE has no formal machine semantics; its primitives come
from production kernels and hardware documentation and are validated by
tests over its kernel corpus. <span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Contour</span> instead derives its knobs from
the formal, RTL-lifted machine semantics of the target, and Contour-Ext adds a
knob only after it passes legality checks against these semantics and the
numerical oracle. Third, CAKE’s candidates are written by LLM agents,
whereas the mapping surface of Contour-Explore can be searched by LLM agents and
by conventional policies such as hill climbing and GA alike.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7. </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Contour</span>, a compiler-mediated framework for kernel
generation on emerging accelerators. Contour-Explore connects search policies
to a reusable compiler through a workload-specific mapping surface: the
compiler completes partial mapping intents into legal plans, generates
target code, and returns verified correctness and performance feedback.
Contour-Ext extends this surface when search stalls: an extension agent
implements a new knob and its lowering, and Contour-Ext keeps the knob only if
it passes correctness and effectiveness checks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The naive agent searching through Contour-Explore returns a correct
kernel on every instance, whereas KernelCraft returns one on only
60% of the 20 Gemmini instances and 5 of the 18 PLENA instances. On the
instances where KernelCraft succeeds, the Contour-Explore agent’s
kernels are <math id="S7.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.86\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.86</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.86\times</annotation></semantics></math> (Gemmini) and <math id="S7.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.13\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.13</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.13\times</annotation></semantics></math> (PLENA) faster than
KernelCraft’s, and Contour-Explore spends 26.3% and 83.4% fewer
tokens per correct kernel. The Contour-Explore agent’s kernels are also
<math id="S7.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.17\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.17</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.17\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than Gemmini’s library routine and <math id="S7.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.46\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.46</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.46\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster
than those of the PLENA compiler. AccelOpt finds <math id="S7.p2.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.50\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.50</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.50\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster
kernels on Gemmini and
<math id="S7.p2.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.20\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.20</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.20\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster kernels on four PLENA attention instances when it
searches through Contour-Explore instead of editing kernel programs. On 16 VTA instances,
Contour-Ext extends the AutoTVM surface, and AutoTVM’s XGBTuner finds
<math id="S7.p2.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4.14\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.14</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.14\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster kernels on the extended surface; on PLENA, the extended
surface makes the kernels found by hill climbing <math id="S7.p2.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.20\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.20</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.20\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster.
These results show that partial mapping specification
with compiler completion lets neural and conventional search share one
verified interface, and that this interface can be extended when search
stalls.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A future direction is recursive improvement across data, models, and
harnesses, inspired by MetaRSI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al., 2026</a>)</cite>. The verified kernels,
mapping decisions, and measured performance produced by Contour-Explore,
together with the knobs accepted by Contour-Ext, could serve as post-training
data. A post-trained model could then search more efficiently and propose
further knobs; once these knobs pass the checks of Contour-Ext, they would
expand subsequent searches and produce further training data.</p>
</div>
</section>
